plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 21: The Second Law of Thermodynamics
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets four cylinder-and-piston drawings side by side as the successive steps of a cycle. Each cylinder holds a gray region stippled with dots for the gas, capped by a piston whose stem rises from the open top, and each stands inside a large colored block representing its surroundings. In the first, a red block labeled "Reservoir" and "(Temperature Th)" sends a thick gray arrow Qh upward into the gas while a green arrow W1 points up from the piston stem. The second sits in a pale block labeled "Insulation", green arrow W2 pointing up and the gas column taller. The third stands in a blue "Reservoir" block marked "(Temperature Tc)", with a green arrow W3 pointing down onto the piston and a gray arrow Qc leaving downward. The fourth returns to an "Insulation" block, with W4 pointing down and the gas at its shortest column. Bold captions run beneath: "Step 1: Isothermal expansion", "Step 2: Adiabatic expansion", "Step 3: Isothermal compression", and "Step 4: Adiabatic compression", each followed by a transition written M to N, N to O, O to P, and P to M. Left to right, block color, arrow direction, and gas volume shift together to track where heat crosses the boundary and which way work is done. The sequence lays out the four processes of the Carnot cycle for an ideal gas.

interactionPlan.concept: The Carnot cycle is a sequence of four reversible processes — isothermal expansion, adiabatic expansion, isothermal compression, adiabatic compression — in which heat crosses the system boundary only during the two isothermal steps while the gas is in contact with a reservoir, while the insulated adiabatic steps shuttle the gas between the two reservoir temperatures.
elements: four side-by-side cylinder-and-piston panels, one per step, all four always visible
saturated red surroundings block for step 1, label 'Reservoir' centered at the block bottom with '(Temperature Th)' beneath it
pale neutral insulation block for step 2, label 'Insulation' centered at the block bottom
saturated blue surroundings block for step 3, label 'Reservoir' centered at the block bottom with '(Temperature Tc)' beneath it
pale neutral insulation block for step 4, label 'Insulation' centered at the block bottom, fully rendered
centered white cylinder cut into each block, gray gas region stippled with dots inside
gas column heights: tall in steps 2-3, medium in step 1, shortest in step 4
piston as a darker gray horizontal cap closing the top of each gas column, with only a short stubby handle tab above it
thick gray heat arrow Qh pointing upward into the gas in step 1
thick gray heat arrow Qc pointing downward out of the gas in step 3
green work arrows W1 (up) and W2 (up) beside the pistons of steps 1-2
green work arrows W3 (down) and W4 (down) beside the pistons of steps 3-4
bold captions: 'Step 1: Isothermal expansion (M→N)', 'Step 2: Adiabatic expansion (N→O)', 'Step 3: Isothermal compression (O→P)', 'Step 4: Adiabatic compression (P→M)'

interactions.label: Cycle step
interactions.teaches: The four processes happen in a fixed order — expansion then compression — and each step changes the gas volume, the work direction, and whether heat flows, returning the system to its starting state M

interactions.label: Boundary condition
interactions.teaches: Heat crosses the boundary only when the cylinder sits in a reservoir (steps 1 and 3, Qh in and Qc out); inside insulation (steps 2 and 4) no heat flows and temperature change comes entirely from work — toggling highlights all panels matching that boundary type without changing the selected step

demo_steps.title: Step 1: Isothermal expansion (M→N)
demo_steps.narration: The cylinder sits in the hot reservoir at Th. Heat Qh flows in and the gas expands at constant temperature, pushing the piston up and doing work W1 on the surroundings.

demo_steps.title: Step 2: Adiabatic expansion (N→O)
demo_steps.narration: Now surrounded by insulation, no heat can cross the boundary. The gas keeps expanding and lifting the piston (W2 up), but the energy comes from its own internal energy, so it cools from Th to Tc.

demo_steps.title: Step 3: Isothermal compression (O→P)
demo_steps.narration: In contact with the cold reservoir at Tc, work W3 is done on the gas and the expelled energy leaves as heat Qc, keeping the temperature constant while the volume shrinks.

demo_steps.title: Step 4: Adiabatic compression (P→M)
demo_steps.narration: Insulated again, work W4 compresses the gas with no heat exchange; the compression work warms it back from Tc to Th, returning it exactly to state M and closing the cycle.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Heat flows only during the two isothermal steps (Qh in at Th, Qc out at Tc) while the insulated adiabatic steps merely shuttle the gas between those two temperatures — the surroundings block under the cylinder, not the piston motion, tells you whether heat can flow.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Faithful four-panel reconstruction of the source figure only — no p-V diagram, no invented curves or constants. Four vertical panels in a row, each a tall colored block with a centered white cylinder cut into it. Block fills must be saturated: a strong warm red for the hot reservoir (step 1) and a strong cool blue for the cold reservoir (step 3), not washed pastels; insulation blocks (steps 2 and 4) a pale neutral beige. Block labels ('Reservoir' / 'Insulation', plus '(Temperature Th)' / '(Temperature Tc)' for reservoirs) are centered horizontally at the bottom of each block, with enough bottom padding that no text is clipped — verify the step-4 'Insulation' label renders in full. Gas is light gray with a dense dot stipple; the piston is a darker gray horizontal cap on top of the gas column with only a short stubby handle tab protruding upward — not a long rod spanning the cylinder. Heat arrows thick and gray (Qh up into the gas in step 1, Qc down out of it in step 3); work arrows thinner and green beside the pistons (W1, W2 up; W3, W4 down). Gas column heights rank step 2 ≈ step 3 (tallest) > step 1 > step 4 (shortest). Bold black captions centered under each panel: step number and process name, then the (X→Y) transition. The stepState button highlights the active panel (full saturation, emphasized arrows) and dims the others. The thermalContact toggle must NOT change stepState: it only emphasizes which panels share the selected boundary type (e.g. 'Isothermal' highlights panels 1 and 3 with a colored outline) while the currently selected step stays selected.

plan.reconstructionNotes: Four vertical panels in a row, each a tall colored block filling most of the panel height with a centered white cylinder cut into it. Block colors: warm red (step 1), pale neutral beige (steps 2 and 4), cool blue (step 3). Gas rendered as a light gray fill with a dense random dot stipple; piston as a darker gray horizontal cap with a narrow vertical stem. Heat arrows thick and gray, work arrows thinner and green, placed beside the piston stem. Arrow directions: W1, W2 up; W3, W4 down; Qh up into the gas; Qc down out of it. Gas column heights rank step 2 ≈ step 3 (tallest) > step 1 > step 4 (shortest) to reflect the volume changes. Bold black captions centered under each panel in three lines: step number and process name, then the (X→Y) transition. Only the active step's panel is fully saturated and its arrows emphasized; inactive panels dimmed. For the p-V path view, replace the four panels with a single p-V axes plot: two smooth convex isotherm curves (upper labeled Th, lower labeled Tc) connected by steeper adiabat segments, corner points M (high p, low V), N, O (low p, high V), P marked with dots and labels, small clockwise arrowheads along the loop, and the segment matching the current stepState drawn thicker and brighter.

Block labels ('Reservoir' / 'Insulation', plus '(Temperature Th)' / '(Temperature Tc)' for reservoirs) are centered horizontally at the bottom of each block, with enough bottom padding that no text is clipped — verify the step-4 'Insulation' label renders in full. Gas is light gray with a dense dot stipple; the piston is a darker gray horizontal cap on top of the gas column with only a short stubby handle tab protruding upward — not a long rod spanning the cylinder. Heat arrows thick and gray (Qh up into the gas in step 1, Qc down out of it in step 3); work arrows thinner and green beside the pistons (W1, W2 up; W3, W4 down). Gas column heights rank step 2 ≈ step 3 (tallest) > step 1 > step 4 (shortest). Bold black captions centered under each panel: step number and process name, then the (X→Y) transition. The stepState button highlights the active panel (full saturation, emphasized arrows) and dims the others. The thermalContact toggle must NOT change stepState: it only emphasizes which panels share the selected boundary type (e.g. 'Isothermal' highlights panels 1 and 3 with a colored outline) while the currently selected step stays selected.
